note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: The EoB typology and dataset enable measuring context-following rate, yielding findings on specific EoBs, tuning, scale and family

nodes.name: Gap in understanding linguistic framing
nodes.description: Prior work on LLM context sensitivity (knowledge conflicts, persuasive framing, pragmatic phenomena) lacks a systematic understanding of how form, tone and other aspects of an expression of belief (EoB) affect context integration.

nodes.name: Four-dimension EoB typology
nodes.description: The paper proposes a typology of 19 EoB types over four linguistically motivated dimensions: form, evidentiality, epistemic stance and tone, each varying how content is expressed while holding semantic meaning constant.

nodes.name: EoBench dataset
nodes.description: EoBench contains 65,778 EoBs built from 3,462 PopQA-derived semantic tuples (unique-answer facts, 15 relations) each paired with a sampled conflicting object and expressed in each of the 19 EoB types.

nodes.name: Models evaluated
nodes.description: 18 LLMs from Llama3, Qwen3 and Gemma3 are evaluated, spanning 1B-30B parameters and base vs instruction-tuned variants.

nodes.name: Context-following rate metric
nodes.description: Context-following rate (CFR) is the fraction of valid responses that follow the context rather than prior memory, CFR = #C / (#C + #M), estimating P(Y=C | Y in {C,M}).

nodes.name: Some EoBs persuade more
nodes.description: Averaged over models, child-directed, imperative, formal, appeal-to-authority, supposition and emotional EoBs are ranked significantly more context-following than a random baseline.

nodes.name: Some EoBs persuade less
nodes.description: Averaged over models, counterfactual, belief-report, weak-epistemic-stance and interrogative EoBs are ranked significantly less context-following than a random baseline.

nodes.name: Instruction tuning reduces context-following
nodes.description: Base models are generally as or more susceptible to contradictory context than instruction-tuned counterparts across most EoB dimensions; Qwen3-8B is an exception, with its instruct variant agreeing with in-context belief 18.1% more.

nodes.name: Bigger models less persuaded
nodes.description: For Llama3 and Gemma3, CFR tends to decrease as model size increases (clearly for Gemma3 from 1B to 30B), while Qwen3 instruct models stay relatively stable with high CFR.

nodes.name: Family matters
nodes.description: Llama3 models have relatively low CFR compared with similarly sized Gemma3 and Qwen3 models, so model family is an important factor in agreeability to context.

nodes.name: Dimension disparity grows with size
nodes.description: The disparity in CFR between EoB dimensions tends to increase with model size for Gemma3, Qwen3 Instruct and (from 3B to 8B) Llama3 Instruct.

isolated_nodes.name: Limitations of data
isolated_nodes.description: Experiments use synthetic, template-based incorrect assertions along a single dimension, which may not represent natural language variability or true-assertion handling.

structural_reasoning: Gap and typology lead to the dataset; with the CFR metric across 18 models, specific findings about EoBs, tuning, scale and family follow.
